plan.summary: A minimal Express.js server exposing a single greeting route. No authentication exists; the goal is to add JWT-based user authentication (register, login, and a protected route).

phases.name: Analysis & Research
phases.description: Understand the current codebase and research the JWT authentication approach and required dependencies.

tasks.description: Analyze the existing project structure (index.js, package.json, README.md) to document current routes, middleware, and dependencies.
Research current best practices for JWT auth in Express: recommended libraries (jsonwebtoken, bcryptjs), token storage, expiry, and middleware patterns. Document the chosen approach.

phases.name: Planning
phases.description: Define the authentication architecture, API endpoints, data model, and security decisions.

tasks.description: Design the auth architecture: in-memory user store (no DB in project), password hashing with bcryptjs, JWT issuance with jsonwebtoken, and middleware for route protection. Define API endpoints: POST /register, POST /login, GET /protected.
Define security and config decisions: JWT secret via environment variable with fallback, token expiry (e.g., 1h), password hashing rounds, and error handling strategy.

phases.name: Implementation
phases.description: Implement dependencies, auth routes, middleware, and wire everything into the server.

tasks.description: Add dependencies jsonwebtoken and bcryptjs to package.json and run npm install to lock them.
Create src/auth.js with an in-memory user store, registerUser (hash password with bcryptjs), authenticateUser, and signToken/verifyToken helpers using jsonwebtoken.
Create src/middleware/authMiddleware.js with an authenticateJWT middleware that validates the Authorization Bearer token and attaches the user to req.
Create src/routes/authRoutes.js with POST /register and POST /login handlers returning JWT tokens, and a protected route (GET /protected) using the auth middleware.
Refactor index.js to add express.json() middleware, mount the auth routes, keep the existing root route, and read JWT secret from environment with fallback.
Add tests (jest + supertest) covering register, login, invalid credentials, missing/invalid token on protected route, and successful token access.
Update README.md with setup instructions, environment variable documentation, and API endpoint examples.

phases.name: Review & Verification
phases.description: Review the implementation for correctness and security, and verify the app runs and tests pass.

tasks.description: Review all auth code for security issues: password hashing, JWT secret handling, token expiry, error responses (no leaking internals), and input validation.
Run npm test and npm start to verify the server boots and all tests pass; fix any bugs found during verification.
